newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan Taleban to allow TV, but only Islamic.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban to allow TV, but only Islamic.

text.p: The Taleban Islamic movement, which rules more than two-thirds of Afghanistan, said on Saturday it would soon lift its ban on television, but would allow only broadcasts conforming to Islam.
"The Islamic state and the Taleban movement are not against television, but are against programmes contrary to the Islamic Sharia law," a Taleban government spokesman said.

Mirza Mohammad Yousufzai, chief of inspection and supervision for the Department for the Promotion of Virtue and Suppression of Vice, told reporters that the future television broadcasts would be based on Sharia. "There will be documentary and artistic programmes adapted to Sharia."
He gave no date for the resumption of television broadcasts.

The Taleban banned television in the capital Kabul when it captured the war-shattered city last September, driving out the government of president Burhanuddin Rabbani. It has also stopped music on the state radio, calling it un-Islamic, and banned women from working and going out of their homes without wearing an all-embracing "burqa" veil.

The Kabul television building has come under frequent shelling by armed factions during their struggle for the control of the capital in the past four years after the collapse of a communist government.
Most windows of the building are broken and most equipment has either been destroyed or taken away as booty by one faction or the other.
The ousted government had allowed Iranian, Japanese and some classic movies on Kabul television and also allowed women to work as announcers and producers.
But the Taleban banned television completely.

As Kabul celebrates the festival of Eid al-Fitr on Sunday, the movement has emphasised that women can venture out during the three festival holidays only if they wore "burqa" veils. People have also been warned against organising dog-fights and cock-fights during the Eid.
"Our mobile groups are patrolling the city and trangressors will be punished," a government announcement said.
